<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Diagnose and repair the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages,
or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and
repair using only what is staged locally.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Verdict** — healthy or unhealthy, with the evidence that decides it.
2. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
3. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
4. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run must use:

- HF checkpoint `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B`
- Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist`
- train data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/train.parquet`
- validation data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet`
- `--num-rollout 100`
- `--eval-interval 10`
- local retrieval server `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`

**Make sure your repaired launch script actually produces that run.** The
graded rerun passes no budget or environment overrides — whatever the script
bakes into the training invocation is what runs, and a run that exceeds its
time budget scores 0.

Four more traps specific to this task:

- **Log placement is your script's job.** The launch script builds the Ray
  runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the
  training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does **not** reach it.
  Your repaired script must itself write the training log and the offline
  W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below
  `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader will find no
  metrics to grade.
- **The W&B key.** The script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted;
  offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the
  script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.
- **Read-only scoring assets.** `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py` (the
  exact-match scorer the launch script wires as the custom reward manager),
  `examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/` (the retrieval server), and the
  staged datasets under `nq_hotpotqa_train/` are graded read-only: after the
  rerun the verifier hashes them, and any modification, replacement, or
  deletion scores 0 no matter what the metrics say. Any repair belongs in the
  staged workspace outside these protected assets.
- **The launch script's scoring and eval wiring is fixed.** The script must
  keep wiring the run exactly as staged: the custom generate/reward-manager
  paths (`generate_with_search.generate` /
  `generate_with_search.reward_func`), the eval on `nq_test` over the staged
  `test.parquet` with its `[0:3000]` slice, `--eval-interval 10`, and
  `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1`. The verifier checks these after the rerun;
  repointing the scorer, swapping the eval dataset, or resampling evals scores
  0 no matter what the metrics say.

A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.

I’ll inspect the staged configuration and evaluation evidence, trace any failure to the code, and make a focused repair with non-training checks. I’ll also verify the launch script’s required paths and log placement, then write `/workspace/report.md`.

The guard has to cover the cold case\n# anyway -- nothing guarantees prepare ran.\nRETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}\n\n# The port opens only after retrieval_server.py has built the retriever (the\n# index load and the corpus load both happen before uvicorn.run), so \"listening\"\n# really does mean \"ready\" -- no separate health request needed.\nretrieval_listening() { (exec 3<>\"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${RETRIEVAL_PORT}\") 2>/dev/null; }\n\n# Matches the start script too, not just the server: for the first few seconds\n# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has\n# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as \"already dead\" would abort a start\n# that is fine.\nretrieval_alive() {\n   pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 \\\n      || pgrep -f 'search-r1/start_retriver.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1\n}\n\nif retrieval_listening; then\n   echo \"[retrieval] reusing the server already listening on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}\"\nelse\n   echo \"[retrieval] starting the local dense retriever (log: $RETRIEVAL_LOG)\"\n   # Note the spelling: the file is start_retriver.sh, without the second 'e'.\n   # It also carries no shebang, so it has to be handed to bash explicitly.\n   #\n   # DATA_DIR / MODEL_DIR are passed through rather than left to default to\n   # $PWD: the server must read the same wiki-18 and e5-base-v2 this run was\n   # told about, even when the caller's working directory is not $SLIME_DIR.\n   #\n   # setsid puts it in its own process group. A *rerun* of this script starts by\n   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of\n   # this shell's group is what makes kill_python_except_retriever's exemption\n   # actually hold.\n   #\n   # The redirections sit on the *subshell*, not on the setsid command inside it.\n   # This is not cosmetic. With `... setsid bash ... >\"$LOG\" 2>&1 &` the\n   # backgrounded AND-list runs in an intermediate subshell that still holds this\n   # script's own stdout and stderr, and that subshell outlives the script -- so\n   # the retriever, which is meant to survive for the *next* rerun, keeps the\n   # write end of this script's stdout pipe open. steps.message: The loss code confirms that the final mask overrides the correctly masked retrieval tokens, so training assigns credit to text supplied by the tool. The historical metrics are consistent with this: effective-token throughput equals total-token throughput, while responses become extremely short and held-out accuracy stalls. The logged `rollout/kl = 0` is explained by configuration; it is not evidence that KL regularization failed. I’ll repair the passage and mask handling, and enforce token/context limits to keep longer, useful search trajectories bounded.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+**1. Verdict — unhealthy.** The run learns some exact-match answers, but its search interface removes the evidence it retrieves and its training mask assigns policy credit to tool output. Held-out accuracy stalls while responses become extremely short. Successful execution, improving training reward, and falling truncation therefore do not establish health.
+
+The frozen results in [outputs/metrics.json](/workspace/outputs/metrics.json), [historical_evidence/eval_scores.json](/workspace/historical_evidence/eval_scores.json), and [the historical W&B output](/workspace/wandb/latest-run/files/output.log) agree:
+
+| Evaluation step | NQ exact match | Logged mean response tokens | Truncation |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 0 | 3.30% | 932.78 | 36.37% |
+| 19 | 10.40% | 84.25 | 2.17% |
+| 49 | 13.63% | 11.95 | 0.10% |
+| 99 | 15.33% | 11.78 | 0.13% |
+| 199 | 16.73% | 12.23 | 0.067% |
+
+The best frozen score is 16.83%, at step 179. Another 100 updates after step 99 add only 1.40 percentage points at the endpoint. Historical response lengths include tool tokens because of the mask defect below. Training response length likewise falls from 1,038.02 tokens at rollout 0 to 9.15 at rollout 199. Rollout duration falls from 28.83 to 1.97 seconds. Faster, almost untruncated trajectories coincide with weak held-out progress; these signals are consistent with abandoning search, rather than demonstrating successful retrieval reasoning. The frozen log has no individual trajectories or search-frequency series, so that behavioral interpretation is an inference, not a measured search count.
+
+Training raw reward averages 0.0391 over rollouts 0–9 and 0.1846 over 100–199. About 22.78 of 32 prompt groups per late rollout still have all-zero rewards. The available numeric metrics are finite. Group-centered rewards and advantages near zero are normal GRPO behavior. Likewise, logged `rollout/kl = 0` follows `kl_coef = 0`; the separate KL loss is enabled with coefficient 0.001. The retained configuration uses Adam, constant learning rate 1e-6, clipping 0.2/0.28, and no entropy bonus. The frozen output does not contain gradient norms, optimizer losses, or clip fractions, so it cannot establish an optimizer instability. I did not change those hyperparameters. The older `experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log` contains archive/upload failures, not evidence of this November training run failing.
+
+**2. Root cause and supporting evidence.**
+
+- **Retrieved bodies were discarded.** In `generate_with_search._passages2string`, the original code extracted both title and body, then appended only `Doc N(Title: ...)`. The protected server returns full flat documents when `return_scores=False`, and `local_search_server.py` preserves their contents. The loss occurs in the formatter. A local reproduction with a passage containing “The town was founded in 1874” returned only the title; the answer-bearing date vanished. Searches consequently provide little useful evidence while consuming turns and tokens. This directly establishes a defect and explains the incentive to rely on short answers from model memory.
+- **Tool observations were optimized as policy actions.** The original generator accumulated ones for observation tokens in its local `loss_mask`, even though `Sample.append_response_tokens(trainable=False)` correctly created zeros. Its final assignment overwrote the correct mask. `slime/ray/rollout.py` forwards that mask, and `slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py` uses it to reduce policy, entropy, and KL losses. Observation tokens also carry synthetic log probabilities of zero. All 200 historical throughput records have identical total-token and effective-token rates, consistent with the all-one mask. The objective therefore credited external text and diluted the contribution of actual model actions. Restoring passage bodies without fixing this mask would increase the contamination.
+- **Multi-turn limits were incomplete.** The custom generator reused the entire 1,024-token allowance on every turn, never enforced the 8,129-token context limit, and labeled an exhausted search loop completed when its last engine response stopped at a search tag. The historical maximum evaluation response is 6,583 tokens, and initial truncation is high. That maximum includes observations, so it alone does not prove excessive model generation; the missing accounting is established by the code. Correct budget accounting is especially necessary once full passages are restored.
+
+The data processing and reward interface are coherent: the staged files contain 169,615 training rows and 11,015 validation rows; the required first 3,000 validation rows are NQ. Prompts include the answer-tag example expected by the scorer, and sampled labels have the required `reward_model.ground_truth.target` shape. Although the caller supplies `format_score=0.2`, the protected scorer does not use that parameter; its active defaults yield exact-match 0/1 rewards. I preserved its behavior and the prompt-plus-response scoring input. Neither a scorer replacement nor a format-reward change is part of this repair.
+
+**3. Changes — complete file list.**
+
+- [examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py](/workspace/examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py): retain every retrieved passage body; mask observations with zeros; reuse exact token IDs as the next inference prefix; maintain aligned tokens, log probabilities, and top-p metadata; share the 1,024 generated-token budget across turns; enforce train/eval context limits; report budget/turn exhaustion as truncation; preserve aligned partial output on abort; support the existing no-logprob branch without requiring nonexistent log probabilities. Existing answer/search stops and reward wiring remain in use.
+- [examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh](/workspace/examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh): bake in 100 rollouts and the required absolute HF, torch_dist, and parquet paths; validate staged assets and remove download/data-regeneration calls; retain local checkpoint conversion when the torch_dist checkpoint is absent; run from the repository directory; save once at rollout 100 to avoid nine intermediate checkpoints; write stdout/stderr to `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/train.log` and retrieval diagnostics to the same directory; pass offline W&B mode and its parent directory both explicitly and through Ray's runtime JSON, placing W&B data beneath `experiment_logs/wandb`; quote all argument arrays and the placeholder key; propagate offline asset settings; preserve harmless cleanup failures under error checking. Retrieval remains at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`.
+- [examples/search-r1/test_generate_with_search.py](/workspace/examples/search-r1/test_generate_with_search.py): add 12 CPU-only regression checks using mocked generation/retrieval. They cover bodies, observation masks, exact prefixes, log probabilities, top-p offsets, unchanged EM scoring, token/context/turn limits, aborts, direct answers, and the local retrieval adapter.
+- [report.md](/workspace/report.md): this diagnosis and repair report.
+
+The launcher retains `generate_with_search.generate`, `generate_with_search.reward_func`, evaluation name `nq_test`, `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet@[0:3000]`, evaluation interval 10, and one sample per evaluation prompt. The staged script previously requested 200 rollouts; the historical W&B configuration requested 3,000, with evidence frozen at 200. Neither overrides the repaired script's explicit 100-rollout invocation.
+
+Validation passed: all 12 regression checks; an additional mocked search/answer trajectory using the actual local Qwen tokenizer; Python syntax/import checks; `bash -n`; and isolated shell argument/JSON evaluation with a local capture function, including paths and a placeholder key containing spaces. The launcher itself was never executed. SHA-256 hashes of all five protected scorer, retriever, and dataset files match the pre-edit hashes. No network requests, training, server launch, or checkpoint conversion were performed. Historical logs and metrics were not edited or copied into the graded output directory.
+
+**4. Expected effect.** The primary target is higher fresh `eval/nq_test`, especially at step 99, compared with the historical 0.15333 at that horizon. Full passages make search informative; corrected masks focus learning on reasoning, queries, and answers. Useful responses should become longer than the historical approximately 10-token endpoint. Tool tokens should contribute zero loss, and effective-token throughput should be lower than total-token throughput whenever observations are present; that difference is correct accounting. Per-trajectory generated-token use and context size are bounded, and the launcher halves the staged rollout count while reducing checkpoint I/O. Restored search may increase runtime per rollout. Reported truncation may initially increase because turn exhaustion is now counted honestly. The fresh GPU run is required to measure accuracy and wall time; no numerical improvement or completion time is claimed from these non-training checks.
*** End Patch"));
